mission: Ben and Talon arrive on Iresh. The Foundation/Vigil expedition is already present under legitimate cover. The book’s texture shifts from Coruscant conspiracy to strange-world expedition: wind, pale cliffs, dark water, chimes, black reeds, thin settlement lights, suspicious locals, and too much quiet. A local contact sends them to Sela Dray. Before they ask for help, the reader sees Sela in the middle of ordinary local responsibility: repairing a chime line, arguing over supply access, helping a neighbor, fixing a path marker, or dealing with someone asking about Tavi. Sela refuses Ben and Talon at first because offworlders have already harmed her home. Tavi Dray is missing after taking Foundation money or pressure to guide the expedition. The Foundation has blocked paths, ignored local warnings, brought armed security, and disrupted supply/transport access. Sela eventually agrees to help because finding Tavi and stopping the offworlders overlap.
why_now: The Foundation/Vigil expedition is already on-planet and moving toward the Glasswell. Every day Ben and Talon spend without local knowledge is a day Aevyn gets closer to the cache.
conflict: Ben and Talon need Sela's knowledge of Iresh's paths and dangers, but Sela has already watched one set of offworlders bribe, pressure, and break her home — and Tavi followed the Foundation's money into the exclusion zone. She has no reason to trust two more strangers with urgent purposes.
turning_point: Sela agrees to help — on her terms, not theirs.
closing_hook: Sela agrees to help — on her terms, not theirs.
setting: Iresh — a remote wind-scoured world. Ben and Talon arrive at the small Iresh settlement: pale stone houses, metal chimes hung between roof posts, a fishery on the bay, the constant cold wind. Sela Dray's home and the settlement common ground. The Foundation/Vigil expedition camp is visible in the distance under a Foundation-branded canopy. Black reed marshes stretch toward the cliffs.
emotional_trajectory: Let Iresh breathe, but keep the goal clear. Talon should hate the quiet and joke badly about it. Sela is not a guide function. She is a local who knows exactly how offworlders are breaking her home. Reader-onboarding / grounding note: Iresh is a place before it is a metaphor. The enemy is already here, the locals are wary, and Ben/Talon need local help. Use concrete local harm, not abstract grievance. Sela speaks in survival rules, not Force theory.

stakes.personal: Ben has come this far off-grid, having broken Talon out of prison and burned Saba’s offered review process — if he cannot get local help and fails to stop Aevyn, everything he has already cost himself and others will have been for nothing.
stakes.interpersonal: Sela is the first person on Iresh who will decide whether Ben is another offworlder breaking her home or a different kind of problem. Her conditional trust — based on shared interest in Tavi — is the only alliance available, and it is fragile from the first word.
stakes.external: The Foundation camp is already visible in the distance under its branded canopy. The enemy is operational; Ben and Talon have no map, no local knowledge, and no time to establish their own cover before the expedition reaches the Glasswell.

sensory_details: Cold wind that never stops — not dramatic gusts but a flat, patient pressure that finds every seam in clothing. The smell of black reeds and standing water from the marshes below the cliffs. The thin metallic note of settlement chimes swaying overhead while Sela works a frayed line, hands moving without looking, her attention already on Ben.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Sela names the specific harm the Foundation did — blocked fishing paths, cut chime-lines, Greyline checkpoints near the reed marshes, supply leverage used to pressure Tavi — and Ben does not argue or minimize it. He just asks where Tavi went.
turning_point_detail.shift: Sela realizes Ben is not trying to recruit her for an offworlder cause; he wants Tavi back for her sake as much as for his own mission. Her refusal softens into conditional terms.
turning_point_detail.cost: Sela's help comes with her rules, not Ben's. She will not guide them into taboo ground on Ben's schedule, and she makes clear she will pull them out if the risk to locals increases.

emotional_arc.start: Ben arrives with urgency and a plan — get local help, locate the camp, find Aevyn — and treats the meeting with Sela as a logistics problem to solve quickly.
emotional_arc.shift: Sela's refusal and the specificity of the harm she describes force Ben to slow down and actually hear what has already been broken here. He is not the first person to arrive with good reasons.
emotional_arc.end: Ben accepts Sela's terms without argument, but the acceptance is genuine — he understands he is on her ground and her rules are the only ones that will keep people alive.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Talon arrive on Iresh and a wary local contact directs them to Sela Dray.
key_beats.state_change: They gain a name and a direction but no goodwill — the contact's wariness signals that offworlders are already unwelcome.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the pull to move fast against the friction of not yet being trusted; impatience held back by deliberate deference

key_beats.beat_description: They find Sela mid-task — repairing a chime line the Foundation's Greyline team cut for 'equipment clearance' — and she does not stop working when they introduce themselves.
key_beats.state_change: Sela establishes from the first moment that her attention is on the work, not the visitors — Ben is already on her terms.
key_beats.pov_reaction: slight recalibration; he had a script and she has not looked up yet

key_beats.beat_description: Sela refuses and names concrete local harms — cut chimes, blocked paths, a pressured guide, Tavi gone — treating Ben's Jedi credentials as one more offworlder reason to be suspicious.
key_beats.state_change: The refusal is categorical and specific; Ben's authority-based approach has no purchase here.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the specific discomfort of a good argument landing from an adversarial direction; no counter available, just the need to hear it

key_beats.beat_description: Ben names Tavi and does not argue with Sela's grievance, letting it stand without minimizing it.
key_beats.state_change: Sela's refusal softens into conditional terms — shared interest in Tavi is the only ground they have.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the discipline of holding still when the instinct is to fix; relief that the silence worked

key_beats.beat_description: Sela agrees to help on her conditions: her pace, her routes, her call if locals are endangered.
key_beats.state_change: The alliance is made but Ben is not in charge of it — he has what he needs and it costs him the lead.
key_beats.pov_reaction: acceptance without resistance; the recognition that this is the only kind of help that will actually work here

canon_elements_needed: Iresh physical geography and local survival rules
